dedupe_keys.name: improving the reproducibility and provenance of urban drainage data with renku a platform for sustainable data science and models

description: Jörg Rieckermann and Co-UDlabs colleagues report three applications of the RENKU data-and-code platform to urban-drainage research. The examples cover sediment research, sensor calibration and validation using UDMT, and automated sewer-defect classification using open asset data. RENKU records dataset and processing provenance so that derived information can be traced through these workflows. This record represents the documented demonstrations, while the related UDMT and sewer-defect-model entries represent the scientific tools. Zenodo provides the conference paper freely under CC BY 4.0. Coverage includes three documented modelling workflows, but the native summary does not identify every experiment location, workflow repository or execution environment. It also cautions that provenance tooling does not solve all reproducibility problems. A limitation is that the simulation workflows were not executed, dependency versions were not tested and no source-code or data bodies were fetched.
